settings.question: Are all-season tires safe for Calgary winters?
settings.answer: Not really, if we're being honest. All-season tires handle light snow and cold rain, but their rubber compound hardens below 7°C and they're not 3PMSF-rated for the mountain winter-tire mandate (Oct 1 – Apr 30 on Highway 93 and the Trans-Canada). For drivers who mostly stay on plowed major roads and garage-park, they can work paired with cautious winter driving — but for true Calgary cold, ice, or mountain trips, a dedicated winter tire or a 3PMSF all-weather is the safer call.

settings.question: How long do all-season tires last in Calgary?
settings.answer: Premium touring all-seasons (Michelin Defender 2, Continental TrueContact Tour, Bridgestone Turanza QuietTrack) carry treadwear warranties of 80,000 to 130,000 km — the longest-wearing tires on the market. In real Calgary use, expect 5 to 7 years on a typical sedan or crossover. Rotating every 10,000–12,000 km significantly extends life. Pothole damage from spring freeze-thaw is the biggest cause of early replacement.

settings.question: What's the difference between all-season and all-weather tires?
settings.answer: All-season tires are NOT 3PMSF-rated and aren't legal as winter tires on Alberta's mountain highways. All-weather tires ARE 3PMSF-rated — same winter certification as dedicated winter tires — and can be run year-round. If you want one set of tires year-round that meets the mountain winter-tire rule, all-weather is the answer. If you're running dedicated winters Nov–Mar, an all-season works for the warm months. See our all-weather guide for the year-round picks.

settings.question: Do I still need winter tires if I have premium all-seasons?
settings.answer: If you drive in Calgary winters at all — yes. Even the best all-season (Michelin Defender 2, Continental TrueContact Tour) is significantly outperformed by a dedicated winter tire below -10°C. Stopping distances on packed snow can be 30% longer. Most Calgary drivers either run dedicated winter tires Nov–Mar OR switch to 3PMSF all-weather year-round. All-season alone is fine for someone who garage-parks and avoids deep winter driving — not someone who commutes daily in real Calgary cold.

settings.heading: What an "all-season" tire actually is
settings.intro:
Despite the name, all-season tires aren't designed for true winter conditions. They're optimized for the temperatures between 7°C and the heat of summer — quiet, comfortable, long-wearing, and predictable in dry and wet. Below 7°C, the rubber compound hardens and grip drops sharply.

For most Canadian markets that covers 7–8 months of the year. The other 4–5 months — Calgary's actual winter — are when an all-season tire is a compromise.
settings.outro: If you spend the winter mostly on plowed major roads, garage-park your vehicle, and don't see mountain trips in deep winter, an all-season can work — paired with cautious driving in the worst conditions. If you want a single set that's legal for the mountain winter-tire mandate, look at the all-weather category instead.
